data.cultural_impact: The name Suhbani carries a warm, friendly and inviting vibe. In the Islamic culture, having close companions or sitting in the company of friends (Suhbah) is of great importance. Sufis also stress the importance of associating with the good company, as it helps in the spiritual and moral growth of an individual. Therefore, the name Suhbani, which means 'one who sits with friends', embodies the spirit of companionship, warmth and hospitality that is deeply rooted in Islamic culture.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual context, the name Suhbani holds deep significance as it emphasizes the importance of cultivating strong and meaningful relationships. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is reported to have said, 'The strong is not the one who overcomes the people by himself but the strong is the one who controls himself while in anger'. Companionship, as described by the Prophet (peace be upon him), is an essential tool for controlling anger and overcoming temptations. It is said that 'a strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than a weak believer, and both are beloved to Him in the same way, but he (the strong one) is a protection for himself and for his religion.' Therefore, being a Suhbani, a friend to all, serves as a reminder to always be a source of strength and support for others, as well as a means for personal moral and spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: Suhbani bint Salim, a renowned Sufi Saint and scholar of the Chishti Order. Born in 1544 in India, she became a disciple of Baba Bulleh Shah. Her most significant contribution to the Sufi tradition is her spiritual guide, 'Makkan-ul-Masnavi'. She passed away in 1607.
historical_references.context: Sufi Saint and scholar of the Chishti Order in India

historical_references.reference: Suhbani, one of the wives of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). She was the daughter of Al-Zubayr ibn Al-Awwam and was married to the Prophet (PBUH) in the 6th Hijri year (around 628 CE) following the Battle of Khaybar. There is a Hadith in which the Prophet (PBUH) spoke about her virtues and her reward in Paradise.
historical_references.context: One of the wives of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) in early Islamic history
